# 3. Tấn công — đòn thường + đòn kỹ năng, mỗi đòn một ảnh 3 hướng (144 lính)

> Sinh tự động bởi `docs/art/prompts/gen_prompts.py` (dữ liệu lấy thẳng từ `packages/core`). Sửa ở script rồi chạy lại
> `python3 docs/art/prompts/gen_prompts.py`, đừng sửa tay file này.

- Ảnh lưu theo hệ ở `docs/art/topdown/<hệ>/` (tên ghi cạnh từng prompt), cạnh `rigs.json` của hệ đó.
- Mỗi kiểu chuyển động **một ảnh 3 hàng** (hàng 1 ngang quay **trái**, hàng 2 trước, hàng 3 sau): `<lính>-idle.png`,
  `<lính>-walk.png`, `<lính>-run.png`, `<lính>-attack.png`, `<lính>-skill.png`.
- Luôn **đính kèm bảng 4 mặt** (`<lính>-views.png`, tạo ở file 1) của chính lính đó để giữ đúng màu, tóc, đồ, cỡ pixel.
- `build_topdown_sprite.py` tự nhận ảnh 3 hàng `<lính>-<kiểu>.png` và các ảnh `<lính>-<kiểu>-side|front|back.png` có đủ 3
  hướng thành `anim.<kiểu>`. Nhìn ngang AI lỡ vẽ quay phải thì khai `"flip": ["left"]` cho kiểu đó trong `rigs.json`.
- Xem trước khi dùng: đủ khung, các khung không chạm nhau, cùng cỡ, chân cùng một vạch đất, **mọi khung cùng một hướng**,
  nền trong suốt thật (không phải ô caro vẽ giả). Sai thì tạo lại, đừng cố cứu.

Mỗi lính 2 prompt, mỗi prompt **một ảnh 3 hàng × 6 khung** (hàng 1 ngang quay trái, hàng 2 trước, hàng 3 sau):

1. **Đòn thường** theo loại lính và vũ khí thật trong game (chém, đâm hai nhát, bắn cung, ném lao, nổ súng,
   phóng máy…). Lưu `<lính>-attack.png` → `anim.attack`.
2. **Đòn kỹ năng** theo đúng kỹ năng riêng của lính trong `packages/core/src/skills.ts`, hiệu ứng theo hệ:
   - kỹ năng đòn đánh (`strike`): **chí mạng** (×1.5 trở lên) hoặc **đòn cường hoá**: vũ khí tụ năng lượng hệ, khung ra đòn to hơn
     đòn thường, kèm hiệu ứng (choáng, làm chậm, hất lùi, thiêu / độc / chảy máu, phá giáp, hút máu, lan vùng…);
   - hào quang (`pulse`), gượng dậy khi sắp chết (`low`), bùng lên khi hạ địch (`kill`), nổ / gọi quân khi chết (`death`),
     chuyến vàng may mắn (`haul`), ban phước trạm (`built`).
   Lưu `<lính>-skill.png` → `anim.skill`. Khung ra đòn ghi ở từng mục phải khớp mốc ra đòn của game.

Hướng trước / sau: chân đứng vững, chỉ tay, vũ khí, áo và hiệu ứng chuyển động, đòn đánh diễn ra ngay trước thân người.
Thợ mỏ gõ vào mỏ vàng, thợ xây gõ vào trạm: **không vẽ mỏ / trạm** trong ảnh lính (chúng có prompt riêng ở
`4-ban-do.md`), chỉ vẽ dụng cụ dừng ở chỗ chạm cùng mảnh vàng / tia lửa bắn ra.

## 1. ☀️ Thánh Quang Điện — Temple of Light (hệ Quang)

Hiệu ứng của hệ: *golden-white holy light: solid pixel sun rays, a bright four-pointed star and a thin golden sun ring*.

**1. Thợ mỏ** (×0.9) — kỹ năng **Phúc lành** (Blessing): khi máu dưới 40%: hồi 50% máu, giảm 50% sát thương nhận

*Đòn thường 3 hướng* → đính kèm `docs/art/topdown/light/miner-views.png`, lưu thành `docs/art/topdown/light/miner-attack.png` (3 hàng × 6 khung: ngang / trước / sau, ra đòn khung 5)

```
Pixel art sprite sheet: ONE image, 3 rows x 6 columns (18 equal frames, evenly spaced, nothing touching another frame; frames about 61 x 43 px native per frame), a 6-frame ATTACK animation (room for the weapon at full reach) of the SAME character as in the attached model sheet. Row 1 = SIDE view facing LEFT, row 2 = FRONT view, row 3 = BACK view; frames go left to right in time order; within a row the feet stay on one ground line at the same spot (in place, no travelling).

ONE DIRECTION PER ROW (the most important rule)
- Row 1: SIDE view, strict profile facing LEFT in EVERY frame: head, chest, hips and feet all point LEFT; only ONE eye visible at the left edge of the head; the face never turns toward the viewer; never two eyes, the face turning toward the viewer, facing right, a front or back view.
- Row 2: FRONT view, facing the viewer straight on in EVERY frame: both eyes visible, chest and hips square to the viewer, the body left-right symmetrical apart from the held gear, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing down the screen; never a profile, a single eye, the head or body turned sideways, a back view.
- Row 3: BACK view, the back to the viewer in EVERY frame: no eyes, no face and no profile visible, shoulders and hips square, the cloth covering the back, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing up the screen; never any eye or face, a profile, the head or body turned sideways, a front view.
- Every frame of a row is a redraw of that row's model view; between frames only the arms, the weapon, the cloth and the effects (and the legs in row 1) change. Nobody turns, nothing switches to another view, no 3/4 angle.
- Final check before finishing, count the eyes in every frame, the LAST frame of each row included: row 1 = ONE eye in all 6 frames, row 2 = TWO eyes (the face) in all 6 frames, row 3 = NO eyes (the back) in all 6 frames. Fix any frame that breaks this; never let a row end in another view.

CHARACTER (Temple of Light civilization, Light element, gold miner "Miner"), identical in all 18 frames: same colours, gear, size and pixel scale
- Build: chibi stickman with a big round head (about a third of the total height) and a short body, slightly smaller and leaner, about 90% of a normal stickman. Size: about 18 x 18 px footprint, about 32 px tall.
- Head: big spiky glowing golden hair with a bright white four-pointed star in it, bold pixel clusters hugging the head. Black face, no mouth, no nose; slanted glowing golden eyes (2-pixel clusters with a white core pixel): TWO eyes in the front view, only ONE eye at the front edge of the head in the side view, no eyes in the back and top views.
- Body: solid black body with thin glowing golden crack lines on the limbs, a small brown cloth gold sack with a golden drawstring on a strap at the hip, gold nuggets peeking out.
- Cloth: short scarf in rich gold (#e8a91c), ragged stepped pixel edges, hanging close to the body.
- Gear: glowing pickaxe; every glowing part in radiant gold (#ffd84a).
- Pose: tool resting on the shoulder in one hand, relaxed.

GEAR LOCK (check every one of the 18 frames)
- Always drawn, complete, same size and same colours in EVERY frame: glowing pickaxe; a small brown cloth gold sack with a golden drawstring on a strap at the hip.
- The weapon / tool stays in the same hand; when the body hides part of it, the visible ends still show. A frame without the weapon or tool is wrong.

ACTION
- Row 1 (SIDE view, strict profile facing LEFT, redrawn from cell 2 (SIDE view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) ready: the pickaxe resting on the shoulder, the gold sack at the hip.
2. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) lift: both hands raise the pickaxe off the shoulder.
3. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) wind-up peak: the pickaxe high over the head, body leaning back.
4. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) swing: the pickaxe sweeps down in front, body leaning forward.
5. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) IMPACT: the pickaxe strikes the gold mine standing just in front (the mine is a separate map sprite: do NOT draw it); the tip stops in mid-air at waist height, knees bent, a burst of solid gold chips and sparks at the tip, one gold nugget popping out.
6. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) COLLECT: the pickaxe back on the shoulder, the free hand drops the nugget into the gold sack, the sack now fuller.
- Row 2 (FRONT view, facing the viewer straight on, redrawn from cell 3 (FRONT view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) ready: the pickaxe resting on the shoulder, the gold sack at the hip.
2. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) lift: both hands raise the pickaxe off the shoulder.
3. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) wind-up peak: the pickaxe high over the head, body leaning back.
4. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) swing: the pickaxe sweeps down in front, body leaning forward.
5. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) IMPACT: the pickaxe strikes the gold mine standing just in front (the mine is a separate map sprite: do NOT draw it); the tip stops in mid-air at waist height, knees bent, a burst of solid gold chips and sparks at the tip, one gold nugget popping out.
6. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) COLLECT: the pickaxe back on the shoulder, the free hand drops the nugget into the gold sack, the sack now fuller, still the FRONT view with the face and both eyes like frame 1 of this row (NOT the back view of the row below).
- Row 3 (BACK view, the back to the viewer, redrawn from cell 4 (BACK view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) ready: the pickaxe resting on the shoulder, the gold sack at the hip.
2. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) lift: both hands raise the pickaxe off the shoulder.
3. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) wind-up peak: the pickaxe high over the head, body leaning back.
4. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) swing: the pickaxe sweeps down in front, body leaning forward.
5. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) IMPACT: the pickaxe strikes the gold mine standing just in front (the mine is a separate map sprite: do NOT draw it); the tip stops in mid-air at waist height, knees bent, a burst of solid gold chips and sparks at the tip, one gold nugget popping out.
6. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) COLLECT: the pickaxe back on the shoulder, the free hand drops the nugget into the gold sack, the sack now fuller, still the back view like frame 1 of this row.
- Row 2 (front) and row 3 (back) play the same beats at the same time as row 1, read flat with no turning: the pickaxe rises and strikes the unseen mine in front of the body, gold chips flying at the tip; there 'forward' means down the picture in front of the body (row 2) or up the picture, partly hidden by the back (row 3); the legs keep a planted stance.
- Frame 5 is the moment of the hit in all three rows and must read clearly.
- The weapon is ONE solid object in every frame, never cut, never bent.

STYLE
- Chunky pixel art: every art pixel a crisp square block, upscaled with nearest neighbour.
- 3-tone shading (cool dark shadow, saturated mid-tone, warm highlight), bold 1px dark outline.
- Arms, legs, weapon shafts and staffs at least 2 px thick.
- Glows are solid bright pixel clusters with a white-hot core; every effect is a solid pixel shape touching the body, the weapon or the ground line, nothing floating.
- Strictly orthographic: no perspective, no 3/4 angle.
- Background: fully transparent PNG (alpha). No white, no colour, no checkerboard pattern.

AVOID: text, labels, numbers, grid lines, borders, ground shadow, motion blur, speed lines, glow halo, bloom, gradients, anti-aliasing, 1-pixel thin lines, floating particles, extra limbs, a second weapon, cells of different sizes, the character changing size, a 3/4 head or body turn, the body turning to show a step, a swing or the cloth, realistic or painterly style, 3D render, any row with frames in another view, a missing or half-drawn weapon or tool, dust clouds.
```

```
- Chunky pixel art: every art pixel a crisp square block, upscaled with nearest neighbour.
- 3-tone shading (cool dark shadow, saturated mid-tone, warm highlight), bold 1px dark outline.
```

```
Pixel art sprite sheet: ONE image, 3 rows x 6 columns (18 equal frames, evenly spaced, nothing touching another frame; frames about 68 x 49 px native per frame), a 6-frame ATTACK animation (room for the weapon at full reach) of the SAME character as in the attached model sheet. Row 1 = SIDE view facing LEFT, row 2 = FRONT view, row 3 = BACK view; frames go left to right in time order; within a row the feet stay on one ground line at the same spot (in place, no travelling).

ONE DIRECTION PER ROW (the most important rule)
- Row 1: SIDE view, strict profile facing LEFT in EVERY frame: head, chest, hips and feet all point LEFT; only ONE eye visible at the left edge of the head; the face never turns toward the viewer; never two eyes, the face turning toward the viewer, facing right, a front or back view.
- Row 2: FRONT view, facing the viewer straight on in EVERY frame: both eyes visible, chest and hips square to the viewer, the body left-right symmetrical apart from the held gear, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing down the screen; never a profile, a single eye, the head or body turned sideways, a back view.
- Row 3: BACK view, the back to the viewer in EVERY frame: no eyes, no face and no profile visible, shoulders and hips square, the cloth covering the back, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing up the screen; never any eye or face, a profile, the head or body turned sideways, a front view.
- Every frame of a row is a redraw of that row's model view; between frames only the arms, the weapon, the cloth and the effects (and the legs in row 1) change. Nobody turns, nothing switches to another view, no 3/4 angle.
- Final check before finishing, count the eyes in every frame, the LAST frame of each row included: row 1 = ONE eye in all 6 frames, row 2 = TWO eyes (the face) in all 6 frames, row 3 = NO eyes (the back) in all 6 frames. Fix any frame that breaks this; never let a row end in another view.

CHARACTER (Shadow Cult civilization, Shadow element, standard bearer (buffs allies) "Soul banner"), identical in all 18 frames: same colours, gear, size and pixel scale
- Build: chibi stickman with a big round head (about a third of the total height) and a short body. Size: about 20 x 20 px footprint, about 36 px tall.
- Head: wild purple-black hair whose tips break into solid smoke wisps, bold pixel clusters hugging the head. Black face, no mouth, no nose; slanted glowing ghostly violet eyes (2-pixel clusters with a white core pixel): TWO eyes in the front view, only ONE eye at the front edge of the head in the side view, no eyes in the back and top views.
- Body: black body with a violet tint, the cloth edges breaking into solid smoke wisps.
- Cloth: scarf and a flag of the same colour in deep violet (#3d1a66), ragged stepped pixel edges, hanging close to the body.
- Gear: a tattered ghost flag with a skull emblem held upright in both hands; every glowing part in ghostly violet (#b77bff).
- Pose: holding the flag pole upright, flag hanging.
- Note: The flag is a solid cloth panel at least 3 pixels thick, its pole upright beside or behind the body.

GEAR LOCK (check every one of the 18 frames)
- Always drawn, complete, same size and same colours in EVERY frame: a tattered ghost flag with a skull emblem held upright in both hands.
- The weapon / tool stays in the same hand; when the body hides part of it, the visible ends still show. A frame without the weapon or tool is wrong.

ACTION
- Row 1 (SIDE view, strict profile facing LEFT, redrawn from cell 2 (SIDE view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) ready: flag pole upright.
2. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) lift: the flag raised high in both hands.
3. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) wave 1: the flag swept to one side, the cloth snapping.
4. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) PLANT: the pole slammed down into the ground, a solid shock ring at its base.
5. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) wave 2: the flag rippling wide above.
6. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) recover: back to the ready pose.
- Row 2 (FRONT view, facing the viewer straight on, redrawn from cell 3 (FRONT view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) ready: flag pole upright.
2. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) lift: the flag raised high in both hands.
3. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) wave 1: the flag swept to one side, the cloth snapping.
4. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) PLANT: the pole slammed down into the ground, a solid shock ring at its base.
5. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) wave 2: the flag rippling wide above.
6. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) recover: back to the ready pose, still the FRONT view with the face and both eyes like frame 1 of this row (NOT the back view of the row below).
- Row 3 (BACK view, the back to the viewer, redrawn from cell 4 (BACK view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) ready: flag pole upright.
2. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) lift: the flag raised high in both hands.
3. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) wave 1: the flag swept to one side, the cloth snapping.
4. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) PLANT: the pole slammed down into the ground, a solid shock ring at its base.
5. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) wave 2: the flag rippling wide above.
6. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) recover: back to the ready pose, still the back view like frame 1 of this row.
- Row 2 (front) and row 3 (back) play the same beats at the same time as row 1, read flat with no turning: the flag waves and is planted in front of the bearer; there 'forward' means down the picture in front of the body (row 2) or up the picture, partly hidden by the back (row 3); the legs keep a planted stance.
- Frame 4 is the moment of the hit in all three rows and must read clearly.
- The weapon is ONE solid object in every frame, never cut, never bent.

STYLE
- Chunky pixel art: every art pixel a crisp square block, upscaled with nearest neighbour.
- 3-tone shading (cool dark shadow, saturated mid-tone, warm highlight), bold 1px dark outline.
- Arms, legs, weapon shafts and staffs at least 2 px thick.
- Glows are solid bright pixel clusters with a white-hot core; every effect is a solid pixel shape touching the body, the weapon or the ground line, nothing floating.
- Strictly orthographic: no perspective, no 3/4 angle.
- Background: fully transparent PNG (alpha). No white, no colour, no checkerboard pattern.

AVOID: text, labels, numbers, grid lines, borders, ground shadow, motion blur, speed lines, glow halo, bloom, gradients, anti-aliasing, 1-pixel thin lines, floating particles, extra limbs, a second weapon, cells of different sizes, the character changing size, a 3/4 head or body turn, the body turning to show a step, a swing or the cloth, realistic or painterly style, 3D render, any row with frames in another view, a missing or half-drawn weapon or tool, dust clouds.
```

```
- Row 2: FRONT view, facing the viewer straight on in EVERY frame: both eyes visible, chest and hips square to the viewer, the body left-right symmetrical apart from the held gear, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing down the screen; never a profile, a single eye, the head or body turned sideways, a back view.
- Row 3: BACK view, the back to the viewer in EVERY frame: no eyes, no face and no profile visible, shoulders and hips square, the cloth covering the back, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing up the screen; never any eye or face, a profile, the head or body turned sideways, a front view.
- Every frame of a row is a redraw of that row's model view; between frames only the arms, the weapon, the cloth and the effects (and the legs in row 1) change. Nobody turns, nothing switches to another view, no 3/4 angle.
```

```
ACTION
- Row 1 (SIDE view, strict profile facing LEFT, redrawn from cell 2 (SIDE view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) ready: crouched low, pickaxe ready.
2. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) dig: the pickaxe bites the ground, dirt chunks flying.

4. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) POP-UP: bursting out of the ground in front, pickaxe swinging up.
5. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) follow-through: the pickaxe high above the head, dirt chunks around the feet.
6. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) recover: crouched low again.
- Row 2 (FRONT view, facing the viewer straight on, redrawn from cell 3 (FRONT view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) ready: crouched low, pickaxe ready.
2. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) dig: the pickaxe bites the ground, dirt chunks flying.
3. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) burrow: half the body sunk into a hole in the ground.

3. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) burrow: half the body sunk into a hole in the ground.
4. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) POP-UP: bursting out of the ground in front, pickaxe swinging up.
5. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) follow-through: the pickaxe high above the head, dirt chunks around the feet.
6. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) recover: crouched low again, still the back view like frame 1 of this row.
- Row 2 (front) and row 3 (back) play the same beats at the same time as row 1, read flat with no turning: the tunneler dives into the ground and pops up in front of the body; there 'forward' means down the picture in front of the body (row 2) or up the picture, partly hidden by the back (row 3); the legs keep a planted stance.

- Background: fully transparent PNG (alpha). No white, no colour, no checkerboard pattern.

AVOID: text, labels, numbers, grid lines, borders, ground shadow, motion blur, speed lines, glow halo, bloom, gradients, anti-aliasing, 1-pixel thin lines, floating particles, extra limbs, a second weapon, cells of different sizes, the character changing size, a 3/4 head or body turn, the body turning to show a step, a swing or the cloth, realistic or painterly style, 3D render, any row with frames in another view, a missing or half-drawn weapon or tool, dust clouds.
```

```
- Row 2: FRONT view, facing the viewer straight on in EVERY frame: both eyes visible, chest and hips square to the viewer, the body left-right symmetrical apart from the held gear, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing down the screen; never a profile, a single eye, the head or body turned sideways, a back view.
- Row 3: BACK view, the back to the viewer in EVERY frame: no eyes, no face and no profile visible, shoulders and hips square, the cloth covering the back, like a classic 16-bit RPG sprite facing up the screen; never any eye or face, a profile, the head or body turned sideways, a front view.
- Every frame of a row is a redraw of that row's model view; between frames only the arms, the weapon, the cloth and the effects (and the legs in row 1) change. Nobody turns, nothing switches to another view, no 3/4 angle.
- Final check before finishing, count the eyes in every frame, the LAST frame of each row included: row 1 = ONE eye in all 6 frames, row 2 = TWO eyes (the face) in all 6 frames, row 3 = NO eyes (the back) in all 6 frames. Fix any frame that breaks this; never let a row end in another view.
```

```
- Build: a chibi stickman rider (big round head, about a third of the rider's height) on its mount. Size: about 22 px wide x 44 px long footprint (the mount's length runs along the TOP view's vertical axis), about 44 px tall including the rider.
```
```
- Head: water hair curling in small waves with a few glowing droplets attached, bold pixel clusters hugging the head. Black face, no mouth, no nose; slanted glowing aqua eyes (2-pixel clusters with a white core pixel): TWO eyes in the front view, only ONE eye at the front edge of the head in the side view, no eyes in the back and top views.
```

```
- Cloth: flying cape and a saddle cloth in aqua (#3aa6e6) water ribbons, opaque, ragged stepped pixel edges, hanging close to the body.
- Gear: riding a black silhouette shark with glowing eyes gliding on a solid pixel wave, glowing lance; every glowing part in aqua blue (#6fe0ff).
- Pose: shark surging forward, lance held forward.
- Note: TOP view: the mount's head points DOWN. SIDE view: the mount faces LEFT. Rider sits on the mount's centre line; the mount is a dark silhouette with glowing pixel eyes, fins and the wave under it at least 3 pixels thick.

GEAR LOCK (check every one of the 18 frames)
- Always drawn, complete, same size and same colours in EVERY frame: riding a black silhouette shark with glowing eyes gliding on a solid pixel wave, glowing lance.
- The weapon / tool stays in the same hand; when the body hides part of it, the visible ends still show. A frame without the weapon or tool is wrong.

ACTION
- Row 1 (SIDE view, strict profile facing LEFT, redrawn from cell 2 (SIDE view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
```

```
2. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) surge: the shark lunges forward, the wave crest rising behind it, the weapon starting to glow with aqua water energy.
3. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) level: the lance comes down level at chest height, the weapon now fully charged and wrapped in solid aqua water energy, the eyes flaring.
4. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) CHARGE HIT (EMPOWERED STRIKE): the shark at full stretch, the lance thrust far forward, the rider leaning into it, the hit much bigger than a normal attack, a large solid aqua water energy burst at the impact.
5. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) impact: the shark's belly slaps down on the wave, the lance still forward; the effect shows clearly: solid element wisps flowing from the impact back into the unit's chest (life drain).
6. (SIDE view, profile facing left, one eye) recover: the lance comes back up, the shark settling on the wave.
- Row 2 (FRONT view, facing the viewer straight on, redrawn from cell 3 (FRONT view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) gather: the shark arches on its wave, the rider pulling the lance back.
2. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) surge: the shark lunges forward, the wave crest rising behind it, the weapon starting to glow with aqua water energy.
3. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) level: the lance comes down level at chest height, the weapon now fully charged and wrapped in solid aqua water energy, the eyes flaring.
4. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) CHARGE HIT (EMPOWERED STRIKE): the shark at full stretch, the lance thrust far forward, the rider leaning into it, the hit much bigger than a normal attack, a large solid aqua water energy burst at the impact.
5. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) impact: the shark's belly slaps down on the wave, the lance still forward; the effect shows clearly: solid element wisps flowing from the impact back into the unit's chest (life drain).
6. (FRONT view, both eyes, symmetrical) recover: the lance comes back up, the shark settling on the wave, still the FRONT view with the face and both eyes like frame 1 of this row (NOT the back view of the row below).
- Row 3 (BACK view, the back to the viewer, redrawn from cell 4 (BACK view) of the attached sheet in all 6 frames):
1. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) gather: the shark arches on its wave, the rider pulling the lance back.
2. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) surge: the shark lunges forward, the wave crest rising behind it, the weapon starting to glow with aqua water energy.
3. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) level: the lance comes down level at chest height, the weapon now fully charged and wrapped in solid aqua water energy, the eyes flaring.
4. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) CHARGE HIT (EMPOWERED STRIKE): the shark at full stretch, the lance thrust far forward, the rider leaning into it, the hit much bigger than a normal attack, a large solid aqua water energy burst at the impact.

6. (BACK view, no face, symmetrical) recover: the lance comes back up, the shark settling on the wave, still the back view like frame 1 of this row.
- Row 2 (front) and row 3 (back) play the same beats at the same time as row 1, read flat with no turning: the shark surges up on its wave and the rider thrusts the lance in front of the body; there 'forward' means down the picture in front of the body (row 2) or up the picture, partly hidden by the back (row 3); the legs keep a planted stance.
- Frame 4 is the moment of the hit in all three rows and must read clearly.
- The weapon is ONE solid object in every frame, never cut, never bent.
- SPECIAL MOVE: clearly stronger and flashier than the normal attack, coloured with water: solid aqua wave crests, round droplets and white foam curls (opaque pixels, not see-through).
- Effects may reach the frame edges but stay solid pixel shapes touching the unit, the weapon or the ground line.

STYLE
- Chunky pixel art: every art pixel a crisp square block, upscaled with nearest neighbour.
- 3-tone shading (cool dark shadow, saturated mid-tone, warm highlight), bold 1px dark outline.
- Arms, legs, weapon shafts and staffs at least 2 px thick.
- Glows are solid bright pixel clusters with a white-hot core; every effect is a solid pixel shape touching the body, the weapon or the ground line, nothing floating.
- Strictly orthographic: no perspective, no 3/4 angle.
- Background: fully transparent PNG (alpha). No white, no colour, no checkerboard pattern.

AVOID: text, labels, numbers, grid lines, borders, ground shadow, motion blur, speed lines, glow halo, bloom, gradients, anti-aliasing, 1-pixel thin lines, floating particles, extra limbs, a second weapon, cells of different sizes, the character changing size, a 3/4 head or body turn, the body turning to show a step, a swing or the cloth, realistic or painterly style, 3D render, any row with frames in another view, a missing or half-drawn weapon or tool, dust clouds.
```
